trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the probability move coincides with a concrete headline (Syria/airspace incident) or is pure market drift; scan USD/TRY and Borsa Istanbul futures for confirmation.
time_plan.1h: Compare TUR pre-market/ADR behavior and lira NDFs to the prediction-market move; fade if no corroborating newswire.
time_plan.2h: Assess whether broader EM risk (EEM) is also weak — if so, the signal is macro not idiosyncratic to Turkey.
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate against official Israeli/Turkish government statements and whether de-escalation language appears.
time_plan.12h: Mark TUR return vs entry; note whether move persisted or mean-reverted, and log calibration error for the card.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of a direct Israel-Turkey military encounter is a negative shock to Turkish risk assets. Turkey runs persistent external financing needs and a fragile lira; escalation with a militarily superior, US-backed adversary would trigger capital flight, risk-premium repricing, and lira depreciation that flows directly into dollar-denominated Turkish equity via TUR. Of the two parties, Turkish assets are the more fragile and foreign-capital-sensitive, making TUR the cleaner liquid proxy than Israeli equities.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Confirm whether gold, UST futures, and VIX are moving together (genuine risk-off) or gold is flat.
time_plan.1h: Check real yields and DXY — if the dollar is also bid, the geopolitical gold signal is likely swamped.
time_plan.2h: Re-check whether oil (a more direct regional-conflict proxy) is also rising to corroborate a true escalation read.
time_plan.6h: Reassess if any ceasefire/denial headlines unwind the safe-haven bid.
time_plan.12h: Record gold return and whether it tracked the prediction-market signal at all.

predictions.reasoning: Rising odds of a new Middle East interstate conflict typically bid safe havens. Gold is the most liquid, broadly-traded hedge and would catch a flight-to-safety bid if a NATO member (Turkey) and Israel were credibly heading toward direct force. However the sensitivity is small and gold is driven overwhelmingly by rates/USD, so this is a weak, low-conviction mapping well below the tradable threshold.

evidence_used: Market question on a direct Israel-Turkey military encounter by end-2026, low-base-rate tail event
Turkey's structural external-financing fragility and lira sensitivity to geopolitical risk
Israel-Turkey friction channels (Syria, Eastern Med, airspace) as plausible escalation pathways
General pattern that Middle East interstate escalation bids oil and safe havens while hurting EM assets of the weaker-balance-sheet party
uncertainty_notes: A probability shift in a long-dated (end-2026) market need not imply any near-term 12h asset move; timing mismatch is severe.
Prediction-market liquidity is thin; an implied-probability move may be noise, not information.
Turkey-Israel are not contiguous; actual direct force is hard, so even a probability jump may reflect rhetoric rather than imminent conflict.

llm_justification.summary: A sharp increase in the implied probability of a direct Israel-Turkey military clash would most cleanly pressure Turkish risk assets (TUR lower via lira/risk-premium repricing) and provide a modest safe-haven bid to gold. Turkey, as the more externally-fragile, foreign-capital-sensitive party, is the better liquid proxy than Israeli equities. Both mappings are low-conviction given the long (end-2026) horizon versus a 12h window, thin prediction-market liquidity, and the geographic difficulty of actual direct engagement.
key_assumptions: A material, sharp upward move in the market's implied probability occurred, not just background drift.
The move reflects genuine escalation information rather than prediction-market noise.
Turkish assets react more than Israeli assets due to balance-of-payments fragility.
failure_modes: The event horizon is end-2026; a probability change may have zero 12h public-market impact (timing mismatch), so the move fails to materialize or reverses.
The information may already be public (a known Syria/airspace flare-up), so assets already repriced before the market signal.
TUR is only weakly exposed to a binary, hard-to-execute interstate clash; moves may be dominated by US rates, EM beta, and USD rather than this geopolitical factor.
Gold's geopolitical sensitivity is tiny relative to rates/dollar drivers, making the safe-haven leg likely indistinguishable from noise.
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
